explain.say: On the island of Trinidad there is a lake not of water but of natural asphalt, so firm in places you can walk on it. Most bitumen today comes from the heaviest end of crude oil instead. Mixed hot with crushed stone it becomes asphalt, the black top of most roads. Here is how a hot mix plant makes it.

explain.say: Here is a road in 3D. The top two layers, the surface course and the binder course, are the asphalt this lesson is about: stones glued together with bitumen. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Bitumen grades and Marshall mix design for asphalt roads

explain.say: Bitumen is the black glue; asphalt is the glue plus stone. Bitumen must be soft enough in winter and stiff enough in summer, so it is graded. Look at the groups: a needle test gives penetration grades like sixty seventy; India now uses viscosity grades like VG thirty; America uses performance grades. Which grade suits a very hot desert road: soft or stiff?

Stiff! Now how much bitumen goes in? Engineers make test cylinders at several bitumen contents and crush them in the Marshall test. Look at the stability curve. Too little bitumen and the stones are not glued; too much and they slide on it. Stability peaks here at about twelve point four kilonewtons, near five percent.

explain.say: Now see the air voids curve falling as bitumen fills the gaps. Designers usually aim for about four percent air: enough space for summer expansion, not so much that water gets in. That also lands at five percent, the optimum. Check the voids filled with bitumen: with fifteen percent voids between the stones, VFB is seventy three percent.

faq.q: What is the difference between bitumen and asphalt?
faq.a: Bitumen is the black, sticky binder refined from crude oil. Asphalt, or asphalt concrete, is a mix of bitumen with graded stone and sand, about 5 percent bitumen by weight.
asks: Is bitumen the same as asphalt?

faq.q: What is the penetration grade of bitumen?
faq.a: The depth, in tenths of a millimetre, that a standard needle loaded with 100 grams sinks into bitumen at 25 degrees Celsius in 5 seconds. 60/70 bitumen lets it sink 6 to 7 millimetres; a higher number means softer.
The maximum load a hot, compacted asphalt cylinder carries when squeezed sideways at 60 degrees Celsius in the Marshall test, in kilonewtons. It peaks at a certain bitumen content.

faq.q: How is the optimum bitumen content chosen?
faq.a: From Marshall or Superpave tests at several bitumen contents: usually the content giving about 4 percent air voids, checked against stability, flow and voids filled with bitumen.

faq.q: What is VFB in an asphalt mix?
faq.a: Voids filled with bitumen: the share of the voids between the stones that bitumen fills, VMA minus air voids over VMA. With 15 percent VMA and 4 percent air it is about 73 percent.

facts: Pitch Lake in Trinidad is the largest natural deposit of asphalt in the world.
Bruce Marshall developed the Marshall mix design method at the Mississippi State Highway Department around 1939.

quiz.say: An asphalt mix has 16 percent voids in the mineral aggregate and 4 percent air voids. What is the VFB?
quiz.show: An asphalt mix has VMA = 16% and air voids = 4%. VFB?

wrong.1: That is VMA minus air voids, not yet divided by VMA.
wrong.2: That is air voids over VMA, the unfilled share.

quiz.say: A bitumen with a higher penetration number is…

quiz.why: A bigger number means the needle sank deeper, so the bitumen is softer.

wrong.1: Stiffer bitumen lets the needle sink less.
